# 2026 REBUILT – hindsight

Source: user hindsight notes, batch 1 (2026-09-27).

## Game play / meta
- Two dominant concepts: **4-ball-wide "dumper" shooters** (intake and shooter on opposite sides) and **turrets**.
  Most robots were low, with a passively expanding hopper (the top of the hopper was a flexible net).
- Robots did not spend time climbing: they could score far more points in that time by shooting, so they saved
  the space and complexity.
- **Turrets fed their own zone during their inactive time** (when not playing defense or stealing balls from the
  other alliance), then in the active time cleaned up the fed balls while shooting on the move, and went out to
  cycle once the clean-up was done. **Dumpers** either cleaned up or just cycled.
- **Turrets were better under defense.** Dumpers tried to stay adjacent to walls or field elements so they were
  harder to rotate, but that was not as effective against defense as a turret; their advantage was a very high
  shooting rate.

## Dominant robots
- **4414** – the best robot of the season and the fastest-shooting turret. Low turret robot with a huge,
  passively net-expanded hopper holding about **110 balls** thanks to great space optimization; no other low robot
  could do that (even with the net expanding over the low bar), which gave them a huge advantage.
- **1690, 2056** – very good shoot-on-the-move low turrets with an expanding net and an active roller floor.
- **1323** – another good shoot-on-the-move turret with a dye rotor; not as good as 4414 (smaller hopper, lower
  shooting rate).
- **2910, 254, 27, 9470** – 4-ball-wide shooters with a very high rate: active, continuous roller floor (254: belts)
  feeding an adjustable hooded flywheel (small top wheels to reduce spin). Hopper with a top net that expands
  passively and either flexes under the trench or goes over the bump. 2910 had a hard top (no net), about 50
  balls; the others probably about 60–70. Very effective mass ball intake; shoot on the side opposite the intake.
- **1678** – same as the dumpers above, but with an actively extending hopper (a small telescopic arm extends the
  "roof") to maximize capacity.
- **9483, 4946** – tall turrets with a spindexer or a dye rotor.
- **2481, 1114** – 4-ball-wide, high-rate shooters built for capacity: 2481 about 100+ balls, 1114 about 85. They
  shoot on the same side as the intake, so they can also shoot while adjacent to the HUB. Being easy to defend,
  2481 sometimes came back well before the start of the shift and waited adjacent to the HUB.

## Effective mechanisms
- Ground intakes: 254, 4414, 1690, 2056, 2910, 1114, 27 (some deployed linearly, some flap-down).
- Wide shooters: 2910 and 254 had the best wide shooters of the season.
- 2910 active roller-floor feeding: the fastest wide shooter and feeding of the season.
- 9128 collapsable roof top: instead of flexible everyone used net (which is also effective mechanism), the were a taller robot with floppy very thin polycarb that serve as hopper walls but could flex down under the low bar (103 did the same with brushes). 
- 4414 dye rotor + hopper: the best space optimization and the fastest turret feeding.
- 4414 turret shooter: the fastest single-lane shooter seen so far.
- 1690 / 2056 turrets: very good shoot on the move.
